Putting it in perspective

However you approach fintech, the most durable advantage tends to be process over prediction. Build a plan you can explain in two sentences, automate what you can, review it on a fixed schedule rather than in reaction to headlines, and keep enough liquidity that you are never forced to sell at the wrong moment. None of these steps is glamorous, and none will appear in a highlight reel — but they are the mechanics that separate consistent outcomes from episodic luck.

If you take one thing from this piece, let it be this: the quality of your questions matters more than the quality of your forecasts. Ask what could make you wrong, ask what you are paying for, and ask what would have to be true for your thesis to break. Those three questions will steer you past more mistakes than any indicator, newsletter, or hot tip.
